description: Classifies every public CNA C API declaration on two independent axes. The first is purpose: rules are matched in order against a declaration's header and name and the first match wins, so every route lands in exactly one purpose category and UNEXPLAINED must stay at zero -- a route with no rule is a route nobody has decided about. The second is reachability: which backends actually import the route, measured from the Node adapter's C source and the WebAssembly backend's route table rather than declared here. The two are orthogonal on purpose, because "what is this route for" and "can a consumer reach it today" are different questions and conflating them hides both.

categories.XNA_BACKING: backs an XNA 4.0 member this package projects, reached through a different route or an exact managed implementation
categories.CNA_EXTENSION_BACKING: modern CNA surface outside Microsoft.Xna.Framework, the target of cna-ts/extensions
categories.INTERNAL_RUNTIME_ONLY: runtime plumbing the binding never exposes as public API
categories.MANAGED_BY_DESIGN: XNA value semantics kept exact in TypeScript; routing them through native would add ownership and error paths XNA does not have
categories.TOOLING_ONLY: test, diagnostic and fuzzing hooks that are not application surface
categories.INTENTIONALLY_DEFERRED: real XNA 4.0 surface this package has measured and not yet projected
categories.UPSTREAM_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE: declared by the ABI but with no runtime that answers it on a locally buildable backend

rules.reason: XNA's math, geometry, curve, colour and packed-value semantics are deterministic and are implemented exactly in TypeScript; the differential corpus pins them against the reference implementation. Calling native for them would add a handle, an error path and a backend dependency to operations XNA performs with no failure mode at all.
canonical CNA surface with no Microsoft.Xna.Framework counterpart; it belongs under cna-ts/extensions and never inside the strict XNA projection

backs the Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net session surface, which is projected at zero structural differences and refuses at runtime: a NetworkSession needs a signed-in gamer and a peer, and fabricating either would be worse than the exception XNA raises where the platform is absent

backs the projected Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices types; the adapter reaches this family through the dispatcher's lifetime and the Guide's state, so the rest of it is surface behind an API this package publishes rather than an unbound family
rules.unreachedReason: backs projected GamerServices surface in a header the adapter imports nothing from, so the whole family is measured and deferred rather than partially covered

rules.reason: an _ext route is CNA surface beyond XNA 4.0 by the ABI's own naming rule
the ABI version query is the first route every backend loads and the gate that rejects an incompatible library; it is never public API

backs a projected Microsoft.Xna.Framework member; the adapter already reaches this header's family through at least one imported route, so the remaining declarations are further overloads, accessors and finer-grained spellings of surface the binding covers
rules.unreachedReason: backs projected or projectable XNA surface in a header the adapter imports nothing from, so the whole family is measured and deferred rather than partially covered
